whatItIs.text: Milk fermented by two bacteria — Lactobacillus bulgaricus and Streptococcus thermophilus — whose lactic acid thickens it and gives its tang.

historyNote.text: Yogurt was probably discovered by Neolithic herders in Central Asia and Mesopotamia around 5000 BC, likely by accident; the ancient Greeks ate oxygala with honey (as we eat Greek yogurt now), the word entered English in 1625 from Ottoman Turkish, and Stamen Grigorov identified the bacteria in 1905.

howToChoose.text: Plain, unsweetened yogurt does every job — breakfast to marinade; check for live cultures and short ingredient lists, and pick fat level by use, not by habit.

storage.text: Keep sealed in the fridge and use a clean spoon. The rulebook has the opened-tub window.

foodSafetyRef.note: dairy storage windows live in the food-safety rulebook

useItUp.text: Yogurt bakes into cakes, strains into labneh, or blends into dressings.
